target_customer: Accounting and tax firms (initially UK, now marketed to US firms) that pay for AI agents doing bookkeeping, VAT, payroll, tax and accounts work
problem: Accounting firms are short of staff and spend large amounts of staff time on repetitive compliance workflows across several tools.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to accounting firms, agents priced as an AI coworker

founders.name: Tom Invernizzi
founders.background_notes: Former auditor at Deloitte, then investment banking analyst; applied to the LBS Incubator in 2024 while sketching the idea.

founders.name: Arthur Granacher
founders.background_notes: Wrote Shazam's iMessage app, then about four years at Google DeepMind automating doctor workflows per the LBS article.

competitors.name: Quanta
competitors.what: AI accounting software and bookkeeping automation for firms
competitors.traction_then: not stated in the source I saw

competitors.name: Basis
competitors.what: AI agents for accounting firms working inside existing systems
competitors.traction_then: later sources say about 30 percent of top 25 firms are customers, date unclear

technical_complexity.rationale: Built on foundation models with agent orchestration across QuickBooks, Xero, Gusto and tax tools; the hard parts are integrations and accuracy that a reviewing accountant will accept.

defensibility.rationale: Model capability is shared with every rival; the moat is workflow depth and firm specific learning, which takes time to build.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too early to tell as of late 2026; funded startups such as Basis and Digits were already shipping agents for the same buyer.

market_need_then: Accountancy has a well documented staffing shortage and heavy compliance workload, and 2025 saw a wave of funding into AI for accounting firms.

identity.logo: Plain wordmark seen on the site
identity.mascot_or_character: Product persona named Coco, positioned as a coworker
identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly and human, tagline says Accountants, meet your new coworker

brand_strength.rationale: Young brand with no independent press on the brand itself found; the Coco persona is the one distinctive asset.

outcome_analysis: Combinely is an early stage company that rode the 2025 wave of AI agents for accounting. The CEO is a former Deloitte accountant and the CTO an ex Google DeepMind engineer, which gives founder market fit. It claims 100 plus firms as customers and had raised a seed round by mid 2025. Well funded rivals are the main risk, and the outcome is not yet known.
notes: Funding is only partly verified. Preqin shows a June 2025 seed from Pioneer Fund with no amount. StartupHub lists 2M USD total and Dealroom shows a 500K figure; both are single aggregator claims and unverified. The 100 plus customers figure is the company's own claim. The site did not name founders; names come from the YC page and the LBS article. No outcome news found.
